text: GTA VI is finally here, it has a 99 on Metacritic, and reviewers who played it for over 100 hours
all hit the same problem.
This game does not explain itself, so I read the reviews and the hands-on guides for you,
and I pulled out 13 things GTA VI never tells you.
Quick honesty check, I have not played 140 hours, these come from people who have and
every source is on screen and in the description.
Number 8 is the one that will save your first robbery, and number 13 might save your whole weekend.
Let's go!
Number 1. You can't carry everything anymore.
In GTA 5, your weapon will help an entire army. That's gone.
Early hands-on reports say you get 4 active slots, 2 long guns, 1 pistol, and 1 melee weapon.
Everything else stays in your car or back at your safe house, so you choose your loadout before the mission.
and not in the middle of it.
The good news?
You can swap between your two main guns instantly without even opening the wheel.
Number two, your flipped car will not fix itself.
In the old games, you wiggled the stick and your car rolled back over.
Not here.
But there's a trick.
Walk into the car and keep walking.
A prompt appears, hold square on PlayStation, and you shove it.
Hard.
That flips a car back onto its wheels for free and it even pushes a beached boat
back into the water.
Why does free matter?
Because cars in this game are fragile.
Reviewers keep mentioning repair bills, so stop paying for a tow truck.
Your car door is a weapon?
While you're driving, press square, and you swing the door open into whoever is standing
there.
On a motorbike, it turns into a kick, perfect for knocking a rival off their bike in a race.
You don't just smash the window anymore.
car. To break into a parked car quietly, you use a slim jim. Press triangle to start, then
sweep the right stick from 3 o'clock around to 9 o'clock in one clean move. Do it smoothly
and you're in. No broken glass, no alarm, no witness.
5. There's a hidden car menu. Hold left on the D-pad to bring up the radio. Then push
up on the stick. Now you can roll the windows down, switch on high beams, turn on hazard
lights and drop the roof on a convertible. You can even tap left or right on the d-pad
to use your turn signals. It does absolutely nothing. I love it.
Number six. Click both sticks to find secrets. Press both sticks in at the same time and you
enter focus mode. If something special is close by, you'll see a ring of sound on the screen.
That ring points you to a unique encounter you'd normally walk right past.
So, if you hear something strange, both sticks.
Every time.
The map has a secret color code.
Open your map and look at the buildings.
Dark blue means you can go inside, light blue means you can't.
Rotate the map and you can even find where the doors are.
In a world this big, that saves you hours of pulling on locked handles.

Number 10. You can swim way faster. On the surface, click the stick once for a speed
boost. Click it again for top speed. That burns stamina, so when it runs out, dive.
Underwater the game uses your lungs instead and you keep that top speed for longer.
Number 11. Not every shot is a kill. Watch your hit marker. Red means that enemy
is dead. Yellow means they're only down, still alive, and still on the floor. That
was spotted in Rockstar's own extended look, so in a big fight, yellow is not
finished. Number 12. You can talk your way out. When a stranger gets in your

Borman's mode?
No.
Reviews say it targets 30 frames a second on every console, even the PS5 Pro.
How long is the story?
50 to 80 hours.
Most reviewers landed near 60.
Does your hair grow, like in Red Dead?
No.
You change it at a barber or your safe house.
Is it on PC?
No.
PS5 and Xbox Series only.

And GTA Online? Critics only played the story. Rockstar hasn't shown them in online mode yet.
How big is the download? Huge! PlayStation asks for over 200 gigabytes of free space.
And what is there to do besides crime? Fishing? Golf? Hunting? Diving? Birdwatching? Even drone races?
